title: Immaculate Constellation: the 2024 allegation

lead.text: Immaculate Constellation is the name of an alleged unacknowledged special access programme said to consolidate military imagery of UAP. It reached the public through Michael Shellenberger, who reported an unnamed insider's allegations and brought a twelve-page unsigned report to a House hearing on 13 November 2024; the Pentagon says it has no record of any such programme.

summary.text: The allegation: Shellenberger reported the claims of an alleged government insider that an unacknowledged special access programme has been secretly collecting data on UAP encounters. The report he later delivered is described as naming a parent programme that consolidates imagery and signature intelligence from tasked and untasked platforms, and his written testimony says a source dates its creation to 2017, after the New York Times story on AATIP.

The route: The Debrief published the first general-readership account on 17 October 2024, and four weeks later Chairwoman Nancy Mace entered the twelve-page report Shellenberger had brought into the record of a joint House Oversight hearing.

The response: a Pentagon spokesperson says the Department has no record of the programme and the former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick denies it exists, while a 2025 claimant's account of where he found the name was traced by a critic to wargame documents.

record.text: The hearing of 13 November 2024, a joint sitting of two House Oversight subcommittees chaired by Mace, heard Tim Gallaudet, Luis Elizondo, Shellenberger, listed as founder of Public, and Michael Gold. Its Index of Documents lists a report titled Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation, submitted by Rep. Mace.

Mace said on the record that committee staff had asked her to enter the twelve-page document Shellenberger brought that day, that every member had a copy, and that Burchett would enter it; it was entered without objection.

The document as the committee published it is twelve scanned pages with no author name, classification marking, control number or cover letter. It is a committee repository item and is not printed in the GPO hearing volume, which only lists it.

Its first page says the public version was reviewed and approved for release by the Department of State's Bureau of Global Public Affairs, and that the investigation reached Congress through the whistleblower mechanisms of the FY23 defence and intelligence authorization acts.

The report organises its material into seven categories of evidence, the last of which, Sensitive Sources, consists of a single sentence, and its imagery section catalogues nine incidents headed by the combatant commands they came from.
Asked at the hearing whether he had been read into the programme, Elizondo said he would not be authorised to confirm or deny the existence of any special access programme by name or trigraph.

claimed.text: Shellenberger testified under oath that the report describes a central or parent programme consolidating UAP observations, holding high-quality imagery and measurement and signature intelligence.

He testified to incidents described in it, including orbs forcing an F-22 out of its patrol area, a small orange-red sphere descending over a carrier's flight deck, and a thirteen-minute video of a white orb rising from the sea off Kuwait.

His written testimony says his source called it a strategic intelligence programme and that a source later said it is controlled by the White House and run by DoD to avoid compliance with Title 10. Asked whether he knew the author, he said he did, and declined to say whether his sources were inside the Defense Department.
Mace described the document from the chair as the original document from the Pentagon about a programme the government says does not exist.

Gallaudet testified that a fleet email headed URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE, which carried the GO FAST video, vanished from recipients' accounts the next day, and concluded it must have been classified within an intelligence agency's special access programme; the board sets that beside Shellenberger's account as an inference, not a link.
UAP Gerb alleged in December 2025 that an NRO programme called Sentient supplied overhead imagery and signals intelligence to Immaculate Constellation, established in 2017.

contested.text: The Department's published response is a records statement issued through its press office: "The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION." Former AARO director Kirkpatrick, who had left the office before the report surfaced, has also denied that the programme exists.

On the board's reading a no-record answer is a statement about records, not a denial that a programme exists; the Department has not said the programme does not exist, and no documentary rebuttal has been produced.

A self-identified whistleblower said in 2025 that he found the programme in a folder labelled 2018 Schriever Wargame; Jason Colavito concluded he had apparently mistaken fictitious wargame documents for secret UFO revelations. The board notes that this addresses the 2025 claimant's account, not the provenance of the 2024 report.

The document called a Pentagon report bears no author, classification marking or control number, and says its public version was cleared by a State Department public affairs bureau; the source's identity has not been established.
The board notes that no AARO annual report, statement or PURSUE release has addressed the programme name in the twenty-one months since it entered the record.

questions: Who wrote the twelve-page report, and who is the insider behind it? Shellenberger says he knows the author and protects his sources.
Why does a report described as a Pentagon document say its public version was cleared by the State Department's public affairs bureau?
Has the Department of Defense or AARO ever made a written, non-press response to the report?
Did the report pass through the FY23 whistleblower mechanisms it cites, and what did the receiving offices do with it?
Is the 2025 Schriever wargame account connected to the 2024 document at all, or is it a separate claim about the same name?
